notes: TRANSCRYPTO 2.4: the custom taskbars, Start menus and live scenes run on Microsoft WebView2 inside TRANSCRYPTO's own windows, the volume slider works, and the shells show the signed-in user.

changes.text: The custom shells show the signed-in Windows user: the SharmaJi Command Center menu title and badges, the Orbital core and the Projector avatar use your name and initials

The custom taskbars (SharmaJi, Orbital, Projector), their Start menus and the live scenes now run on Microsoft WebView2 inside TRANSCRYPTO's own windows: no hidden Chrome windows or Chrome processes any more, nothing to find, move or reattach, and a crashed or stuck page restarts by itself
Quick settings volume slider did nothing useful: any move jumped the volume to 100 % (the level was added instead of set). It now sets the exact level, and moving it up unmutes
Files dropped on a taskbar app now reach the engine with their real paths (from anywhere, not only Explorer's selection or the desktop)
Safety: if the custom taskbar's page can't start, the Windows taskbar comes back within 15 seconds instead of leaving you without one
Switching between SharmaJi, Orbital and Projector, their palettes or the live scene only swaps the page: the taskbar window stays, the Windows taskbar no longer flashes up in between
The live scene was torn down and built again at every engine start and every settings change (the static wallpaper was repainted even when no video wallpaper had been running)
